tasks.title: Keep typed values stable across mutable collection aliases
tasks.intent: Repair the reproduced constructor-to-plan validity breach before native-v1 assessment, while preserving valid protocol identities and exact opaque data.
requirements: ObjectValue and ArrayValue must own immutable backing collections so caller aliases cannot invalidate a constructed typed value, including nested payloads and keys.

Shared mutating boundaries must reject invalid programmatic record inputs before producing a writable initialization plan or persisting ledger state; include post-construction changes to borrowed record collections.

Preserve valid canonical hashes, numeric category/scale, Unicode, source provenance and historical evidence. Use typed code without Any, unchecked casts or broad Native Image allowances. No cross-repository authority or implicit operations.
acceptance: Regression cases reproduce mutable alias failures and prove stable values, rejected invalid plans/writes, valid cold reconstruction and unchanged unrelated bytes/mtimes.
Shared JVM/native conformance and packaged process parity pass; old valid hash/evidence witnesses remain unchanged. Record the actual validity boundary and any remaining limits.

roadmaps.title: Protocol value stability
roadmaps.intent: Resolve demonstrated value and input-boundary defects before assessing protocol stability.

review.rationale: The still-open v1 assessment retains every prior gate and gains the demonstrated value-boundary correction. This reviews the future plan only and does not claim implementation or freeze readiness.

evidence.checkpoint: Reviewed docs/proof/value-boundaries/baseline.json and the preserved probe against the new bounded correction contract; all prior prerequisites and historical evidence remain.

assessment.title: Assess native v1 freeze readiness
assessment.intent: Consider v1 only after greenfield, existing-code, legacy-import and remote-backed usage have survived.
requirements: Consider v1 only after greenfield, existing-code, legacy-import and remote-backed usage have survived.
The checkpoint correction gates, including bounded read models and the transitively required planning, provider and timestamp proofs, must be closed/current before assessing native v1.
The reproduced mutable-value/input-boundary defect must be corrected with closed/current TASK.protocol.value-boundary evidence before assessing native v1.
acceptance: Evidence from all four entry paths and complex migrations supports a reviewed protocol freeze decision.
